text:
Honestly, I miss upgrading my PC. Being an enthusiast was fun. Every few years I'd get a growing itch. I enjoyed reading about GPU performance. Looking for the best bang-for-my-budget options. Deciding every few years if I genuinely card about this upgrade cycle or if my components were still good enough.

I never thought I'd miss the FOMO, but when components are at the "I need to seriously weigh this purchase against the value of other significant expenses" this turns from a fun hobby into what starts to feel more like an addiction I need to kick.

I was never in the market for a 5090 at launch, but at that point I was thinking "I could just wait a few years or maybe wait for the price of a 5080 to drop" and now it looks like the 4070Ti I'm running might legitimately be the last and only graphics card I buy this decade, and maybe for the rest of my life. We're palying by completely different rules now and I don't like it.
